notes: Software steps (Arduino Cloud Thing 'TVRemoteController', TV property, Cloud Editor sketch, Alexa skill) are not physical parts and are not in the graph.

Breadboard rows: the image labels the lower half A-E and the upper half F-J, so the lower half is mapped to catalogue bank 't' (rows a-e) and the upper half to bank 'b' (rows f-j). Column numbers are taken from the image labels (30..60). Rail holes are numbered arbitrarily because each rail is a single strip; the lower red-line rail is 'bp', the upper blue-line rail is 'bn'.
The Nano 33 IoT straddles the centre gap: 3V3 is in the top row at column 62 (red wire to the + rail); the bottom-row pins are in row e.

The catalogue lists only A4, A5, GND, 3V3, USB for arduino-nano-33-iot. The IR LED signal pin (column 60) and IR receiver signal pin (column 62) are not labelled in the image and the manual gives no pin number. I assumed D3 (IR LED) and D2 (receiver OUT) as placeholders. The black wire at column 51 is taken as the Nano GND connection to the negative rail, since it is the only way the ground rail reaches the board.

The ir-receiver catalogue entry has no ports, so I used OUT, GND and VCC. From the image the legs are: column 31 to the + rail (VCC), column 32 to the - rail (GND), column 34 to the Nano signal pin via the green wire (OUT).
The IR transmitter is a type 'led'. Its left leg (column 43) goes to GND, taken as the cathode, and its right leg (column 44) goes through the 330 ohm resistor to the Nano, taken as the anode.
The Nano's USB power cable is not shown in the circuit image and is omitted.
